inc-bot: [PAGER] KV cache resident size spike detected on rope-longctx-pool (group rope-pool-06). 3.2x baseline, sustained 5m. Pager level: SEV2. alert_id=kv_resident_spike_2110043210

raj_ops: saw it — lots of longctx requests with NTK ~ 2048, sliding-window prefetch queue growing. Kyv miss rate down, resident set increasing. tagging eng-runtime.

sophia_g (oncall): taking. quick summary pls: which models/routers?

raj_ops: rope-v2 and rope-ntk variants in region-us-west2, traffic routing to rope-pool-06. logs show continuous_batching window=adaptive and prefetch.enabled=true. sample trace: 
```
trace_id=tr-2110043210-7
model=rope-v2-2048
seq_len=1536
ntk=1980
kv_requests=4523
prefetch_queue=184
cache_entries_delta=+180k/5m
```

kevin_runtime: confirmed similar metrics on prom: `sum(kv_resident_bytes) by (pool) increase(5m)` -> +310% on rope-pool-06. heatmap shows many longctx sessions leaking prefetched keys across requests. Likely sliding-window + YaRN heuristic allowing unbounded prefetch when NTK high.

sophia_g (oncall): initial mitigation: throttle prefetch on that pool and reduce continuous_batching max_window. can someone run the guard command?

kevin_runtime: running now: 
```
# throttle prefetch on rope-pool-06
curl -s -X POST https://internal-admin/redwood/infra/pools/rope-pool-06/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}' \
  -d '{"prefetch_rate_limit": 0.2, "continuous_batching_max_window": 128}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra-config/rope-prefetch-throttle -> canary on rope-pool-06 (3 nodes)

anna_prodsec: any customer impact? external SLO errors?

raj_ops: no 5xx spike yet. latency tail (p95/p99) creeping for chat endpoints hitting rope-v2. Might be slow token generation due to cache churn. No reported customer incidents so far. flagging Cx owners to monitor.

eng-ml-lead: recommend also disabling sliding-window prefetch for longctx models until we can bound prefetch by token budget. rolling config change: `sliding_window.enabled=false` for rope-v2* on pool-06.

kevin_runtime: applied sliding-window disable on canary nodes. observing drop in prefetch_queue from 184 -> 12 within 45s. resident growth rate slowed.

sophia_g (oncall): good. escalate? will we need a hotfix?

eng-ml-lead: we should patch YaRN heuristic to cap prefetch based on effective NTK *and* per-request token budget, and add an eviction guard when resident increases > 50% in 1m. I'll open a PR but need runtime team to review.

raj_ops: opening incident ticket and customer-impact sheet. @anna_prodsec @sophia_g please add customer owners.

kevin_runtime: deploy-bot: canary config succeeded, rolling to rest of pool now with 60s stagger.

deploy-bot: rollout complete to rope-pool-06 (30 nodes).

raj_ops: metrics look stable: resident delta now +8% over baseline. p99 latency trending down. no errors.

sophia_g (oncall): handing off to kevin_runtime for followup and postmortem. I'm signing off on-call in 20m. Please include mitigation timeline and next steps in the ticket.

kevin_runtime: taking handoff. action items: 1) follow up PR for YaRN cap (eng-ml + runtime). 2) add automated prefetch throttle when pool resident growth > 2x in 3m. 3) run canary for 24h on staging with synthetic longctx load. 4) notify major customers using rope-v2-2048.

anna_prodsec: any data exfil risk from KV blowup? looks like internal model cache only. no access pattern leak seen. mark as low.

raj_ops: updating incident severity to P2 (no customer-facing errors). creating postmortem placeholder.

kevin_runtime: will coordinate the hotfix PR and sequence (runtime change -> config roll -> telemetry). assigning to @eng-ml-lead and @kevin_runtime. ETA preliminary fix 6h, full rollout 48h.

sophia_g (oncall): thanks all. leaving notes: mitigations applied: prefetch_rate limited, continuous_batching_max_window set to 128, sliding-window disabled, canary roll completed. monitor dash: /dashboards/kv-resident-ropes.

inc-bot: Incident updated: KV cache spike mitigated, status: monitoring. incident_id=INC-2110043210

kevin_runtime: postmortem to include root cause: combination of long-context traffic (NTK>1500), YaRN sliding-window allowing unbounded prefetch per session, and continuous batching config that didn't bound aggregate key set. Remediation: heuristic caps, eviction alarms, and improved telemetry on per-pool prefetch budgets.

sophia_g (oncall): handoff notes posted to ticket. closing thread for now, will reopen if any regressions. :white_check_mark:
